# Micro — Style Reference

> Cool gray blotter, espresso ink, one cartoon ink blot peering over the edge. A black grotesk and a gray nineties serif share each headline on #f5f5f5, drawn with 8%-black hairlines, and saturated color only blinks inside the product.

**Theme:** light

Values are measured from the live site and normalized; names, roles and recommendations are interpretation. Font lists are independent, not paired by position. Example prompts describe reconstructions, not the site's source code.

Micro speaks a two-voice workbench language: a cool #f5f5f5 canvas carries #fafafa product surfaces and #ffffff controls, and every stroke of ink is a warm #221f1c brown-black with #797267 captions. The chromatic budget for the marketing chrome is zero. Saturated color appears only inside the product mockup as status (a #518bdb unread dot, a #e5a057 lightning spark, a #f92d4e alert dot) and in third-party logos. Typography is the thesis: the hero sets a 900-weight Haffer claim beside a gray perfectlyNineties aside inside the same sentence, and section headings switch entirely to the serif at 48px with +0.96px tracking. Below the display tier, hierarchy rides on weight 500 at 14px, the workhorse with 152 uses, rather than on size jumps. Shapes are soft (8px nav buttons, 10px controls, 14px cards), and elevation is a 6.5%-ink ring under a 5% drop. The page reads as a well-kept paper notebook rather than a SaaS dashboard.

## Tokens — Colors

| Name | Value | Token | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Concrete Canvas | `#f5f5f5` | `--color-concrete-canvas` | Body background, section fields and the text on the dark Sign up button, 96 background uses — a cool neutral floor that makes the warm ink read warmer by contrast. |
| Mist Surface | `#fafafa` | `--color-mist-surface` | Automation cards, the agent input and the product-window pane, 77 uses — a 2% lift that separates surfaces from the canvas with value alone, before any shadow arrives. |
| Paper | `#ffffff` | `--color-paper` | Secondary button, announcement pill, nav link capsule and floating widget, 40 uses — the brightest step, reserved for things you click. Do not flood whole sections with it. |
| Quartz Tag | `#f4f4f5` | `--color-quartz-tag` | "Accept" tags on suggestion rows inside the mockup, 4 uses — a tag fill a hair cooler than the canvas, read as a chip rather than a surface. |
| Fog Wash | `#0000000d` | `--color-fog-wash` | Active product tab and the selected "New" sidebar row (estimated placement) — a 5% black wash that marks state without introducing a hue. |
| Ink | `#221f1c` | `--color-ink` | Headlines, body text, logo and the filled Sign up button, 269 text uses — a warm espresso black that keeps the system humane where a #000000 would look clinical. |
| Pebble Caption | `#797267` | `--color-pebble-caption` | Paragraph ledes, timestamps, serif hero asides and metadata, 206 uses — a warm taupe gray that is the second voice of every headline. |
| Ash Hairline | `#00000014` | `--color-ash-hairline` | Input borders, dividers and card edges, 140 uses — an 8% black line that stays visible on both #f5f5f5 and #fafafa without becoming a frame. |
| Stone Border | `#0000001f` | `--color-stone-border` | Secondary button and announcement pill outlines, 3 uses — a 12% black edge rationed to standalone white controls that need to hold their own shape. |
| Cobalt Pulse | `#518bdb` | `--color-cobalt-pulse` | Unread dots beside recent chats in the mockup sidebar, 5 uses — status punctuation rather than decoration. Do not promote it to a link or CTA color. |
| Amber Spark | `#e5a057` | `--color-amber-spark` | Lightning glyphs beside "2h ago" automated threads, 2 uses — marks work the agent did on its own. Keep it to icons at 14px or smaller. |
| Ember Dot | `#f92d4e` | `--color-ember-dot` | Notification and recording dots inside the product mockup, 4 uses — the loudest hue, decorative-only and mockup-internal. Do not use it on marketing chrome. |

## Tokens — Typography

### Haffer — the grotesk that runs the entire interface and shouts the hero claim · `--font-haffer`

- **Substitute:** Inter at 500 for UI (Inter 800 for the 900 hero weight, since Haffer Black draws closer to an Inter ExtraBold), Geist at 500, Instrument Sans at 500. Haffer renders at its nominal weight in the 400–600 range and slightly lighter than nominal at 900, so step down one weight on substitutes only at display size.
- **Weights:** 400, 500, 600, 700, 900
- **Sizes:** 7px, 8px, 10px, 11px, 12px, 14px, 16px, 18px, 20px, 22px, 24px, 28px, 64px (estimated, hero)
- **Line height:** 1.0 (22px), 1.125 (64px, estimated), 1.25 (11px, 28px), 1.333 (12px, 24px), 1.4 (20px), 1.43 (14px), 1.5 (10px, 16px), 1.556 (18px), 1.625 (14px long-form)
- **Letter spacing:** 0.275px at 11px, -0.55px at 22px, -1.6px at 64px (estimated), normal everywhere else
- **Role:** Haffer is the workhorse: 299 elements at weight 500 against 174 at 400, so the medium cut is the default voice and regular is the exception for long paragraphs, which inverts the usual 400-default convention and gives small UI text a confident ink weight. The two 900 instances are the hero claim words only, which makes them the loudest typographic event on the page by a wide margin. Tracking is untouched except at the extremes, slightly tightened at 22px and above and opened on the 11px bold label.

### perfectlyNineties — the serif second voice for asides and section headings · `--font-perfectly-nineties`

- **Substitute:** Fraunces at 600 (optical size 72, softness 0), Young Serif at 400 (single weight that draws heavy enough to match), Newsreader at 600. perfectlyNineties 700 draws slightly lighter than a typical 700 because its contrast is high, so do not use a substitute at 700 or above.
- **Weights:** 600, 700
- **Sizes:** 48px, 64px (estimated, hero aside)
- **Line height:** 1.0 (48px), 1.125 (64px, estimated)
- **Letter spacing:** 0.96px at 48px
- **Role:** A high-contrast nineties serif on an AI productivity site is the anti-convention move — the category default is a tight grotesk at 600. Positive tracking of +0.02em at 48px is the second anti-convention, opening the serif up where most display type gets squeezed, and it makes headings read as editorial captions rather than marketing banners. Its 8 uses make it rationed: it never carries UI.

### ui-monospace — the system mono for uppercase micro-labels · `--font-ui-monospace`

- **Substitute:** JetBrains Mono at 400, IBM Plex Mono at 400, Geist Mono at 400. The native stack renders at nominal weight, and all three match at 10px.
- **Weights:** 400, 500
- **Sizes:** 10px
- **Line height:** 2.4
- **Letter spacing:** 2.2px at 10px
- **Role:** Seventy elements set 10px uppercase mono with +0.22em tracking and a 24px line box — a deliberately technical eyebrow that tags sections the way a filing label tags a folder. Calling the platform mono instead of a webfont signals that this tier is metadata, not brand. The generous 2.4 line height lets labels sit in a row with 14px UI text without shifting the baseline.

### Type Scale

| Role | Family | Weight | Size | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | ui-monospace | 400 | 10px | 2.4 | 2.2px | `--text-small` |
| caption | Haffer | 500 | 12px | 1.333 | 0px | `--text-caption` |
| body-sm | Haffer | 500 | 14px | 1.43 | 0px | `--text-body-sm` |
| body | Haffer | 400 | 16px | 1.5 | 0px | `--text-body` |
| body-lg | Haffer | 400 | 18px | 1.556 | 0px | `--text-body-lg` |
| subheading | Haffer | 400 | 20px | 1.4 | 0px | `--text-subheading` |
| heading-sm | Haffer | 500 | 24px | 1.333 | 0px | `--text-heading-sm` |
| heading | Haffer | 700 | 28px | 1.25 | 0px | `--text-heading` |
| heading-lg | perfectlyNineties | 700 | 48px | 1.0 | 0.96px | `--text-heading-lg` |
| display | Haffer + perfectlyNineties | 900 | 64px | 1.125 | -1.6px | `--text-display` |

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Split every display headline into two voices: the claim in Haffer 900 #221f1c, the aside in perfectlyNineties #797267 at the same 64px — this mid-sentence voice change is the signature of the system.
- Default UI text to Haffer 14px weight 500 with 1.43 line height — 152 uses make medium the baseline, and regular 400 is reserved for paragraphs of 14px and up.
- Keep the chromatic budget at zero outside the product mockup — #518bdb, #e5a057 and #f92d4e appear only as 6–8px dots and 14px glyphs inside the app frame.
- Use #221f1c for every ink element including the CTA fill and logos — the warm brown-black against a cool #f5f5f5 canvas is what keeps the page from reading as a gray template.
- Lift cards with the sm ring `0 0 0 1px rgba(34,31,28,0.065)` plus a 5% drop instead of a solid border — the ink-tinted ring is softer than #00000014 and defines the edge at 14px radius.
- Give the primary button the inset `0 -2px 0 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.2)` keycap edge — this non-negotiable detail is the only tactile cue on an otherwise flat page.
- Track serif headings open at +0.96px on 48px and tighten the grotesk at -0.55px on 22px — opposing tracking directions keep the two voices distinct even at the same size.

### Don't

- Don't set the whole hero in one family at weight 700 — a single-voice headline erases the claim-and-aside rhythm that defines Micro and reads as any AI startup.
- Don't color links, icons or headings with #518bdb because it already exists in the palette — status hues promoted to chrome break the zero-color rule and make the mockup lose its monopoly on color.
- Don't swap #221f1c for #000000 or #111111 on text — pure black on #f5f5f5 turns the warm notebook into a cold spec sheet.
- Don't give automation cards a 24px radius or 32px padding — the system runs 4–10–14–18px, and oversized rounding at 255px card widths turns tiles into toy bubbles.
- Don't apply the xl shadow `0 25px 50px -12px rgba(0,0,0,0.18)` to feature cards — it belongs to the product window alone, and spreading it flattens the single moment of depth.
- Don't tighten the perfectlyNineties headings to negative tracking like a grotesk — the serif voice depends on +0.02em air, and squeezing it at 48px makes the two voices sound alike.
- Never use uppercase Haffer for eyebrows — uppercase is owned by the 10px ui-monospace label with 2.2px tracking, and duplicating it in the grotesk muddies the metadata tier.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**

- canvas: #f5f5f5 (Concrete Canvas)
- card surface: #fafafa (Mist Surface)
- control surface: #ffffff (Paper)
- primary text: #221f1c (Ink)
- secondary text: #797267 (Pebble Caption)
- hairline: #00000014 (Ash Hairline)
- status dot: #518bdb (Cobalt Pulse)
- primary action: #221f1c (filled action)

**Color in Data**

Charts and bars render in #221f1c and #797267 with #00000014 gridlines, and a single series may take #518bdb as a solid fill only when it denotes live or unread status — the marketing page must not let any hue outweigh the black headline.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a hero section on a #f5f5f5 background, centered in a 1152px container with 128px top padding. Place a 32px-tall announcement pill: #ffffff background, 1px solid #0000001f border, 10px radius, padding 4px 12px 4px 4px, a 40×20px thumbnail at left, label "Watch the latest announcement" in Haffer 14px weight 500 #221f1c. 32px below, a two-line headline at 64px with 1.125 line height: the claim words "An agent" and "An everything app" in Haffer weight 900 #221f1c with -1.6px tracking, the asides "to do your work &" and "to manage it" in perfectlyNineties weight 600 #797267. 16px below, a 672px-wide lede in Haffer 20px weight 400, line height 1.4, color #797267. 32px below, a Sign up and Request a Demo button pair with an 8px gap.
2. Build a Primary Action Button: background #221f1c, text #f5f5f5, no border, 10px border-radius, height 44px, padding 0 24px, Haffer 16px weight 500 with 1.5 line height, box-shadow `inset 0 -2px 0 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.2)`. Hover darkens nothing — keep the fill and raise opacity of the inset to 0.3. Pair it with a secondary button: #ffffff background, #221f1c text, 1px solid #0000001f, same 10px radius, 44px height and 0 24px padding, no shadow.
3. Build an automation card grid: four columns in a 1152px container with a 12px gap. Each card has background #fafafa, no border, 14px radius, 16px padding, 192px height, shadow `0 0 0 1px rgba(34,31,28,0.065), 0 4px 6px -1px rgba(0,0,0,0.05), 0 2px 4px -2px rgba(0,0,0,0.05)`. Inside: a 20px outline icon in #797267, 12px gap, title in Haffer 14px weight 600 #221f1c, 4px gap, description in Haffer 14px weight 400, line height 1.625, color #797267. Above the grid, a heading in Haffer 24px weight 500 #221f1c with 1.333 line height.
4. Build a navigation bar 68px tall, transparent on #f5f5f5, not sticky, content in a 1152px container. Left: an 86px-wide wordmark in #221f1c. Center: a #ffffff capsule with 1px solid #00000014 and 10px radius, 4px internal padding, holding links Product, Resources, Pricing, Careers in Haffer 14px weight 500 #221f1c with 4px 12px padding and 8px radius, hover fill #0000000d. Right: "Log in" text link at 14px weight 500 with 0 8px padding, then a 28px-tall Sign up button in #221f1c with #f5f5f5 text, 8px radius, 0 8px padding and `inset 0 -2px 0 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.2)`, separated by 8px.
5. Build a section opener: left-aligned in a 1152px container, 128px above the previous section. A 32px ink-blob mascot glyph in #221f1c, 12px gap, then a heading in perfectlyNineties 48px weight 700, line height 1.0, letter spacing 0.96px, color #221f1c. 12px below, a lede in Haffer 18px weight 400, line height 1.556, color #797267. Optionally place a 10px ui-monospace uppercase label with 2.2px tracking in #797267, 8px above the heading.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Split every display headline into two voices: the claim in Haffer 900 #221f1c, the aside in perfectlyNineties #797267 at the same 64px — this mid-sentence voice change is the signature of the system.
- Default UI text to Haffer 14px weight 500 with 1.43 line height — 152 uses make medium the baseline, and regular 400 is reserved for paragraphs of 14px and up.
- Keep the chromatic budget at zero outside the product mockup — #518bdb, #e5a057 and #f92d4e appear only as 6–8px dots and 14px glyphs inside the app frame.
- Use #221f1c for every ink element including the CTA fill and logos — the warm brown-black against a cool #f5f5f5 canvas is what keeps the page from reading as a gray template.
- Lift cards with the sm ring `0 0 0 1px rgba(34,31,28,0.065)` plus a 5% drop instead of a solid border — the ink-tinted ring is softer than #00000014 and defines the edge at 14px radius.
- Give the primary button the inset `0 -2px 0 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.2)` keycap edge — this non-negotiable detail is the only tactile cue on an otherwise flat page.
- Track serif headings open at +0.96px on 48px and tighten the grotesk at -0.55px on 22px — opposing tracking directions keep the two voices distinct even at the same size.

### Don't

- Don't set the whole hero in one family at weight 700 — a single-voice headline erases the claim-and-aside rhythm that defines Micro and reads as any AI startup.
- Don't color links, icons or headings with #518bdb because it already exists in the palette — status hues promoted to chrome break the zero-color rule and make the mockup lose its monopoly on color.
- Don't swap #221f1c for #000000 or #111111 on text — pure black on #f5f5f5 turns the warm notebook into a cold spec sheet.
- Don't give automation cards a 24px radius or 32px padding — the system runs 4–10–14–18px, and oversized rounding at 255px card widths turns tiles into toy bubbles.
- Don't apply the xl shadow `0 25px 50px -12px rgba(0,0,0,0.18)` to feature cards — it belongs to the product window alone, and spreading it flattens the single moment of depth.
- Don't tighten the perfectlyNineties headings to negative tracking like a grotesk — the serif voice depends on +0.02em air, and squeezing it at 48px makes the two voices sound alike.
- Never use uppercase Haffer for eyebrows — uppercase is owned by the 10px ui-monospace label with 2.2px tracking, and duplicating it in the grotesk muddies the metadata tier.

## Imagery

The page is built from product screenshots rendered as live HTML mockups, not photography. The app window sits on an 18px-radius shell with the xl shadow, and every saturated hue on the page lives inside it: unread dots, lightning sparks, Gmail and Slack glyph colors (mockup-internal, not system tokens), and a circular landscape avatar. Illustration is a single recurring mascot: a black ink-blob character with two oval eyes, drawn in flat #221f1c with no gradients, peeking over the product window in the hero and shrinking to a 32px glyph beside section headings. Icons are 14–20px outline strokes in #797267. No gradients, glows or orbs exist anywhere. The narrative is a friendly creature that does your busywork inside a real, quietly crafted app.

## Layout

Content centers in a 1152px container, with 672px for hero ledes and subtitles. Sections are separated by 128px (96–160px), and the extracted page carries long empty #f5f5f5 stretches between them, so whitespace does the sectioning instead of rules or background shifts. The hero is centered: announcement pill, two-line two-voice headline, a 20px lede in #797267, the Sign up and Request a Demo pair, then the tab strip and a full-width product window overlapped by the mascot. Sections never alternate background color. Automation cards run four columns at 255px, the logo row runs five, and pricing follows the same 1152px grid. The nav is static, transparent and 68px tall: logo left, white link capsule center, Log in and Sign up right. The footer is a 96px-padded open block. At 375px, set the hero at 48px, drop section gaps to 64px and stack cards single-column. Density: comfortable.

## Two-Voice Headlines

The discipline is that every display sentence speaks twice: a 900-weight Haffer claim in #221f1c and a perfectlyNineties aside in #797267, sharing one 64px line box. It breaks the moment someone balances the voices — giving the serif part Ink color, setting both halves in the same family, or making the aside heavier than the claim. It also breaks when the split becomes decorative, with serif words chosen for looks instead of meaning. To extend it, keep the grammar fixed: the noun phrase that names Micro's value goes in the grotesk, and the verb phrase that explains what it does goes in the serif. Section headings may go fully serif at 48px, but no heading goes fully grotesk above 28px.

## Warm Ink, Cool Paper

Micro's neutrals disagree on purpose: the canvas stack (#f5f5f5, #fafafa, #ffffff) is pure, hue-free gray, while every ink value (#221f1c, #797267) leans warm brown. That temperature gap is why a near-monochrome page still feels inviting rather than sterile. It breaks if a builder tints the canvas warm to match the ink, which reads muddy, or cools the text to a slate gray like #64748b, which reads like a default component library. Extend it by deriving any new text tier from #221f1c and #797267 only, and any new surface from pure grays between #f5f5f5 and #ffffff. Borders stay translucent black (#00000014, #0000001f) so they inherit whatever surface they sit on.

## Color Inside The Frame

The chromatic budget is zero on marketing chrome and three status hues inside the product: #518bdb for unread, #e5a057 for agent-initiated work, #f92d4e for alerts. Color is a property of the product, not of the brand, which is why the CTA is Ink rather than a hue. It breaks when a saturated hue escapes the app frame onto a button, link, eyebrow or section background — the mockup instantly stops being the most alive thing on the page. Extend it by adding new status hues only inside product renders, at 8px dots or 14px glyphs, and by keeping each hue bound to one meaning across every screenshot.

## Similar Brands

- **Attio** — shares the CRM-category warm-neutral canvas with near-black ink CTAs and a hero-wide product window as the main illustration; Attio stays single-family where Micro splits headlines into two voices.
- **Notion** — shares a hand-drawn black-ink character system against a quiet gray canvas, with serif display moments on a sans product; Notion's mascots are illustrations, Micro's is a single recurring glyph.
- **Granola** — shares the serif-plus-grotesk pairing on a productivity tool and the warm, unhurried reading tone; Granola leans greener, Micro keeps hue at zero.
- **Superhuman** — shares the email-first product framing and a rationed, keycap-like primary action; Superhuman runs dark and dramatic where Micro sits on light #f5f5f5.
- **Arc (The Browser Company)** — shares the playful-character-meets-serious-tool posture and a floating ambient widget as personality; Arc uses saturated gradients that Micro deliberately refuses.
